### Why `.test-tmp` keeps appearing

`make verify` invokes the `test` target, which runs `cargo test --workspace`: [Makefile](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/Makefile:37) and [Makefile](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/Makefile:72).

The integration-test helper explicitly does this:

1. Creates repo-root `.test-tmp`.
2. Creates each test sandbox inside it with `TempDir::new_in(...)`.

That code is in [common/mod.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/tests/common/mod.rs:398). TUI tests have an equivalent helper in [tui_tests.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/tui_tests.rs:1300).

So `.test-tmp` is created by the tests reached through `make verify`, not directly by Make or Cargo. Successful `TempDir` teardown should remove individual sandboxes; interrupted tests, cleanup failures, or still-running subprocesses can leave `.tmpXXXXXX` directories behind. It previously reached about **38.3 GiB**; after the earlier cleanup it has already accumulated **652 MiB** again.

The immediate story is therefore: active Rust verification accounts for roughly **31 GiB**, Chrome temporary clones account for **38 GiB**, and package/application caches account for tens of gigabytes more. No user Time Machine snapshots were found to explain the loss.
